messages.author: 6b9e76d162900923
messages.subject: specify truncated distributions
parts:
Now I need to specify a truncated distribution, say a half normal, is
it correct to first constrain the variable in the declaration part
(when it is allowed) and then just give it a non-truncated
distribution? Like the following

parameters {
double(0, ) beta;
......
}

model {
beta ~ normal(0, 1);
......
}

Also what is the correct syntax to directly specify a truncated
distribution. Bugs uses I(lb, ub), and Jags uses T(lb, ub).

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] specify truncated distributions
parts:
Yes, that'll work just fine as long as the
bounds are themselves constant. It's a bit
trickier if they're variable.

I went with the JAGS notation T(lb,ub),
but we don't have many of the cumulative
densities implemented, so it's not very general
yet.

- Bob
